title: Belgian PM Bart De Wever offers his government's resignation after budget talks fail
seoTitle: Belgium PM De Wever offers resignation
dek: The five-party coalition could not agree how to find about €10 billion for the 2027 budget. King Philippe has not accepted the resignation and sees De Wever again on 6 November.
happened: On the morning of 2 November, after overnight talks in the core cabinet broke up without a deal, Prime Minister Bart De Wever went to the royal palace and offered his government's resignation. He spent more than an hour with King Philippe and left without speaking to reporters. The palace said the king was taking the decision under consideration.

sides.says: The palace said the king regrets that no agreement was reached on a credible budget and that the country cannot afford a prolonged political crisis. He urged all parties to put the public interest and a willingness to compromise first.

Deputy Prime Minister David Clarinval of MR blamed Vooruit for insisting on higher taxes, and said the last proposal on the table on Sunday evening included more than €3 billion in new taxes. MR and De Wever's N-VA want spending cuts instead of tax rises.

The socialist, Christian Democrat and centrist partners wanted part of the money raised from higher incomes; Euronews puts their target at €1 billion to €1.5 billion. Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said there were "too many sticking points". After seeing the king on 4 November, Vooruit president Conner Rousseau said: "I told the King that we want an agreement", adding that it must be fair and everyone must do their part (translated from French).
Matti Vandemaele of the Greens (Groen) said De Wever "is failing to get his government on the same page".

next: The king has been seeing the coalition party leaders one by one: Sammy Mahdi (CD&V) and Yvan Verougstraete (Les Engagés) on 3 November, Conner Rousseau (Vooruit) and Georges-Louis Bouchez (MR) on 4 November, with N-VA president Valerie Van Peel due on 5 November. De Wever returns to the palace on Friday, 6 November. The king can accept the resignation, which could lead to new elections or a new government from the current parliament, or he can refuse it or wait. Belgian governments have often kept negotiating after offering to resign; in November 2025 De Wever asked the king for more time instead and was given 50 extra days.
summary: Belgium's government is close to collapse over money. The 'Arizona' coalition of N-VA, MR, Les Engagés, Vooruit and CD&V, which took 234 days to form, needs about €10 billion in savings or new revenue for 2027 to bring its deficit back towards the EU's 3% limit; debt is above 110% of GDP. The parties split over whether part of that should come from taxing higher incomes. After the talks failed overnight, Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his government's resignation on 2 November. King Philippe has not accepted it: he has been consulting the coalition leaders since 3 November and sees De Wever again on 6 November.
